arms.note: the baseline. Its rules are NOT to be improved — an improved E2-A stops being a baseline

arms.adds: property canonicalisation: surface forms of one property mapped to a single identifier
extraction into the same {entity, property, scope} schema
deterministic when confident, model only on abstention

prior_art_making_this_urgent: arXiv 2601.00821 finds extraction losing to raw chunks with extraction gaps at 78.8% of failures. If a cheap extractor is the bottleneck rather than the representation, the cheapest possible fix has to be tried before the expensive one, or the conclusion is unreadable
subject: an arm inserted between the rule baseline and the model arm
unchanged: corpus, thresholds, metric definitions, denominators and gates. This inserts an arm and changes no criterion
why: E2-A failed and the first reading of that failure overclaimed. Rules matching the assertion form that records use do not match the interrogative form that questions use — but a canonicalisation layer mapping rotates, rotation, after rotation and old deployment key onto one property identifier could close the same gap with no model. Going straight from failing rules to a model would show that a model works and never that it was necessary
why_that_breakdown: entity 0.99 property 0.96 scope 0.95 address 0.70 would mean the text is understood and the parts are not assembling into a stable address — a different problem from any single accuracy figure, and invisible without the split
